subject: general
question: A trader marked the price of an article so as to earn a profit of 28% on its cost price. He sold it by giving 15% discount on its marked price. What was his actual profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let CP = 100

Actual SP = 128% × 85% × 100

⇒ SP = 128/100 × 85/100 × 100 = 108.8

Profit% = (108.8 - 100)/100 × 100

⇒ Profit% = 8.8

**∴ Actual profit for trader is 8.8%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount % = 15

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Marked price - Marked price × discount%

Profit% = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the article be 100a

So, the marked price to get a profit of 28% 

⇒ 100a + 100a × 28% = Rs. 128a

He is giving a discount of 15%

So, his actual selling price

⇒ 128a - 128a × 15% = 108.8a

So, actual profit = 108.8a - 100a = 8.8a

Profit% = (8.8a/100a) × 100 = 8.8%

**∴ His actual profit is 8.8%.**
